title: '让个人网站成为可以核对的出处'
description: '个人网站的价值不止在发布文章。稳定地址、身份关联和更正入口，可以帮助读者判断一条信息来自谁，也让跨平台传播保留回到原文的路径。'

同一个人的介绍散在几处：社交账号保留着旧公司，活动海报使用曾经的头衔，搜索结果又引用了另一份简介。每一份都像是有出处，合起来却很难判断哪份仍然有效。拥有一个个人网站，首先可以解决一个很小的问题：让别人知道应该回到哪里核对。

第八期讨论了用个人域名定义自己的信息，并通过友情链接相互连接。这是一种可操作的信息组织方式；它能提供作者自己维护的原始说明，但链接数量本身不能证明内容准确，更不能替代对具体事实的核验。

## 先维护那些需要长期引用的信息

个人简介、项目列表、联系方式和重要文章，适合各自拥有稳定地址。更新职位时，修改个人简介页；项目停止维护时，在项目页说明；文章发现错误时，在原文留下更正。这样，外部链接可以继续指向同一个位置，读者也能看到变化。

W3C 关于持久 URI 的说明强调了地址保持稳定的价值。对个人网站而言，这不要求一开始就设计复杂的分类。少把年份、临时组织结构和文件格式绑进永久地址，改版时保留旧地址的跳转，通常比不断重建链接更有帮助。

稳定地址也不意味着正文永远不变。文章的原始发布日期和实质更新日期可以分别保留；涉及事实修正时，说明改了什么。读者需要知道现在的结论，也需要判断之前的引用是否仍然成立。

## 友情链接能表达关系，不能代替背书

链接到另一位创作者，可以表达你愿意介绍这个人，或者觉得他的作品值得看。但这种关系最好有具体对象：某个作者、某项项目、某篇文章。把链接展示为社区导航，比把所有关联都包装成质量认证更准确。

身份关联还有一个容易混淆的地方。普通超链接可以由任何人单方面建立；它不自动证明两个账号由同一人控制。`rel="me"` 是用于表达身份关系的链接约定，验证机制可以进一步检查双方是否相互链接。不同服务如何使用它，仍应看各自的验证规则。

即使身份已经对应，也只能说明账号之间的关系，不能证明文章里的数字、产品能力或消息来源。需要核对的事实仍然要落到具体资料。一个可信的人也可能写错，一篇旧文章也可能已经过时。

## 给转述留一条回到原文的路

假设一篇产品体验被摘成社交平台上的一张图。图片很容易传播，限制条件却可能被裁掉。原文如果有稳定地址，并把使用版本、测试条件和更新说明放在读者容易找到的位置，转述者就能保留一条核对路径。

这也是个人网站对 AI 检索可能有用的地方：清楚的标题、作者信息、时间和来源，让机器与人都更容易理解页面的范围。不过，网站存在、结构清楚或被其他站点链接，都不保证搜索系统一定收录、引用或带来流量。

建设时可以先做好一页准确的自我介绍、一个项目目录，以及少量有完整来源的文章。之后每次更新，检查旧链接是否仍然有效。比起一次放上许多标识，持续维护内容与出处更能让这个地址成为可以依赖的参照。

Someone’s biography is scattered across several places: a social account still names an old employer, an event poster uses a former title, and search results quote another introduction. Each version appears to have a source, yet together they make it hard to tell which information still applies. A personal website can first solve a small problem: giving people somewhere to go to check.

Episode 008 discussed using a personal domain to define one’s own information, with friend links connecting sites. This is a practical way to organize information. It provides an original account maintained by its author, but the number of links cannot establish accuracy or replace checking individual facts.

## Maintain the information people need to cite over time

A biography, project directory, contact details and important articles can each have a stable address. Update the biography when a job changes, explain discontinued maintenance on the project page, and leave corrections on the original article. External links can keep pointing to the same place, while readers can see what has changed.

The W3C’s guidance on persistent URIs explains the value of keeping addresses stable. A personal site does not need an elaborate taxonomy from the start. Keeping years, temporary organizational structures and file formats out of permanent addresses—and redirecting old addresses after a redesign—is often more helpful than repeatedly rebuilding links.

A stable address does not require an unchanging text. Original publication and substantive update dates can be retained separately; factual corrections can explain what changed. Readers need the current conclusion and enough information to judge whether an earlier citation still holds.

## Friend links express a relationship, not a guarantee

Linking to another creator can mean you want to introduce that person or recommend their work. The relationship is clearer when it has a specific object: an author, a project or an article. Presenting links as community navigation is more accurate than treating every connection as certification of quality.

Identity links introduce another distinction. Anyone can create an ordinary hyperlink unilaterally; that does not establish that two accounts belong to the same person. `rel="me"` is a link convention for expressing identity relationships. Verification mechanisms can additionally check reciprocal links, while each service’s rules determine how it uses them.

Even a confirmed identity relationship establishes only the connection between accounts. It does not prove an article’s numbers, product claims or sources. Those still need specific evidence. A trustworthy person can make a mistake, and an old article can become outdated.

## Leave a path from a summary to the original

Suppose a product review is condensed into an image on a social platform. The image travels easily, while its limitations may be cropped out. If the original has a stable address and makes the version, test conditions and updates easy to find, people sharing it can preserve a route back to the evidence.

This is also where a personal site may help AI retrieval: clear titles, authorship, dates and sources make the page’s scope easier for both people and machines to understand. Having a site, organizing it clearly or receiving links still does not guarantee indexing, citations or traffic.

Start with an accurate introduction, a project directory and a few articles with complete sources. Check that old links remain valid as the site changes. Maintaining the content and its provenance over time does more to make an address dependable than adding many badges at once.

同一项工作可能跨过几个工具：在一个 Agent 里调研，在另一个工具里写代码，再用第三个入口整理资料。切换时最费力的部分，往往是重新交代项目进度、找回已经确认的决定，以及分清哪个文件才是最新成果。

第九期谈到，把工作资料集中到 Notion 或 GitHub 等自己选定的位置，再让不同 Agent 使用这些材料。讨论还区分了临时调用的子任务和持续保留的会话。这里的共同问题是：一次任务结束后，下一次工作能否找到足够的依据继续进行。

## 把决定和成果从聊天里取出来

聊天记录保留了讨论过程，却不一定适合作为下一次任务的唯一入口。一个决定可能被反复修改，最后确认的版本埋在很长的对话中。让下一个工具完整重读，既增加消耗，也可能把早已作废的要求重新带回来。

可以先留下几类简单材料：项目的当前目标、已经确认的决定、实际产物的位置，以及尚未完成的问题。比如网站更新完成后，记录上线地址、对应提交和仍在草稿中的文章；下一次修改就能从这些事实开始，而不必重建整段对话。

这些记录最好指向实际文件。写着视频已经导出，还需要对应文件和版本；写着某项测试通过，还需要知道检查的是哪一版。摘要负责帮助定位，原始材料负责支持核对。

## 共用资料需要知道哪些内容可以改

让多个 Agent 访问同一个目录，并不自动产生一致的上下文。假设一个工具还在按旧标题做封面，另一个工具已经修改了文章标题；如果两者都把自己的输出标成最终版，公共目录反而会增加混淆。

一种做法是把可修改的工作稿与已确认的交付物分开，任务开始时说明依据哪个版本，完成时更新当前记录。存在并行修改时，还需要检查冲突。使用 Git 的项目可以借助提交记录核对差异；不使用 Git 的资料，也需要有清楚的版本与恢复方式。

资料组织不必从大型数据库开始。项目很少时，一份索引加若干稳定路径就够用；当关系、状态和查询需求增长，再决定是否需要表格、数据库或专门的界面。节目里也出现了按需临时生成看板的想法，展示形式可以随任务变化，材料本身应当仍然找得到。

## 可迁移还包括权限和备份

把资料集中起来，会同时扩大一次错误操作可能影响的范围。只需要阅读背景的任务，不必获得整个资料库的修改权限；需要调用服务的工具，也不应因为共用上下文就默认获得全部凭据。

GitHub 的认证文档介绍了不同访问方式。实际接入时应按任务选择权限，避免把访问令牌写进会被其他工具读取的普通笔记。具体权限范围还要结合所用应用与接口确认。

可迁移也不能只靠一个远端账号。保存一份能实际恢复的资料副本，明确哪些内容只存在平台内部，比单纯把所有文件搬到同一个服务更有用。备份是否成功，要看能否找回需要的内容，而不只是同步图标有没有变绿。

## 用一次切换检验组织方式

可以选择一项已经完成的小任务，让另一个工具仅凭项目索引、当前决定和成果文件继续修改。检查它是否能找到正确版本，是否还需要重复询问已经确认的事情，以及是否把历史草稿误当成现状。

这次试验若暴露缺口，就补足缺少的记录，而不是把全部聊天无限追加到下一次提示里。值得积累的上下文，是下一次工作确实能使用、能核对，也能在事实改变后修正的材料。

One job can span several tools: research in one agent, code in another, then organize the material through a third interface. Switching often means explaining progress again, finding decisions that were already confirmed and figuring out which file contains the latest result.

Episode 009 discussed gathering work materials in a chosen place, such as Notion or GitHub, and letting different agents use them. It also distinguished temporary subtasks from persistent conversations. The shared question is whether the next piece of work can find enough evidence to continue after the current task ends.

## Extract decisions and results from the conversation

A conversation preserves discussion, but may be a poor sole entry point for the next task. A decision can change repeatedly, with the final version buried in a long exchange. Having the next tool reread everything adds work and may revive requirements that were abandoned.

Start with a few simple records: the project’s current goal, confirmed decisions, the location of actual outputs and unresolved work. After a website update, for example, record the live address, corresponding commit and articles still in draft. The next change can begin from these facts instead of reconstructing the conversation.

Records should point to actual files. Saying a video was exported still needs a file and version; saying a test passed still needs the version that was checked. A summary helps locate the material, while the original supports verification.

## Shared material needs clear editing boundaries

Giving several agents access to one directory does not automatically create consistent context. Suppose one tool is making a cover with an old title while another has already changed the article title. If both label their output final, the shared directory increases confusion.

One approach is to distinguish editable working drafts from confirmed deliverables, state the version a task starts from and update the current record on completion. Parallel edits also need conflict checks. Git projects can use commit history to compare changes; other collections still need clear versions and a way to recover.

There is no need to begin with a large database. For a few projects, an index and stable paths may suffice. As relationships, states and queries grow, consider whether a table, database or dedicated interface would help. The episode also raised the idea of generating a temporary board on demand. Presentation can change with the task while the underlying material remains findable.

## Portability also involves permissions and backups

Centralizing material expands the reach of a mistaken action. A task that only needs background reading does not need permission to modify the whole collection. A tool calling a service should not gain every credential merely because it shares context.

GitHub’s authentication documentation describes different access methods. Choose permissions for the actual task and keep access tokens out of ordinary notes that other tools may read. The appropriate scope also depends on the application and interface being used.

Portability cannot depend on a single remote account alone. Keep a copy that can actually restore the material, and identify what exists only inside a platform. This is more useful than simply moving every file into one service. A successful backup means the necessary content can be recovered, not just that a synchronization icon turned green.

## Test the arrangement with one tool switch

Choose a small completed task and ask another tool to continue it using only the project index, current decisions and output files. Check whether it finds the correct version, asks again about settled matters or mistakes historical drafts for the current state.

If this reveals a gap, add the missing record rather than indefinitely appending every conversation to the next prompt. Context worth accumulating is material the next task can use and verify—and that can be corrected when the facts change.
